Hi Tim and Anna,

Thanks again for the interest — excited to show the Redwood Inference demo next week. We originally suggested a couple slots, but heads-up: Europe moves clocks forward on Sun 29 Mar (CEST starts) and the US already moved in early March. That one-week mismatch can make wall-clock conversions confusing for multi-region calls.

Proposed slots (all shown in local labels to avoid confusion):
- Tue 30 Mar — 09:00 CET / 03:00 EDT / 17:00 JST (tight for APAC)
- Tue 30 Mar — 14:00 CET / 10:00 EDT / 00:00 JST (+1 next day)
- Wed 31 Mar — 11:00 CET / 07:00 EDT / 20:00 JST

Can you confirm which slot works, and whether your attendees prefer the times expressed in their local timezone (we'll send explicit labels)? If none of these work, Laura (cc'd) can propose alternate windows.

I attached a short agenda and will include an .ics once we lock a time.

Thanks,
Aditya

Thanks for the flag, Anna — good question. Short answer: after Sun 29 Mar the correct EU label will be CEST (UTC+2).

To be precise for the slots Aditya proposed (converted):
- Tue 30 Mar — 09:00 CEST (EU) = 03:00 EDT (US) = 17:00 JST (APAC)
- Tue 30 Mar — 14:00 CEST = 10:00 EDT = 00:00 JST (+1)
- Wed 31 Mar — 11:00 CEST = 07:00 EDT = 20:00 JST

We typically see confusion where calendar invites created before the 29th still display CET; we'll create and send an .ics generated with the event timezone set to the host's timezone and explicit UTC offsets in the description so each attendee's calendar maps correctly.

If Anna wants to target a late-morning European slot, recommending Wed 31 Mar 11:00 CEST / 07:00 EDT — this avoids the late-night APAC ripple.

I'll follow up with an invite and a brief mutual action plan.

Laura
